title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: Approximating the genus of cubic graphs is APX-hard.
context_text: In the spherical density regime (graphs with average degree at most 6), there is no evidence of efficient constant-factor approximation algorithms for the genus. The second named author conjectured in prior work (2018) that approximation in this range is hard; the conjecture is stated at the outset to motivate the paper's focus on the dense-graph regime where tractable approximation is possible.
paper_contribution: States the conjecture as background motivation for focusing on the dense-graph regime; the paper does not prove or disprove it.
notes: The attributed author (Mohar, 2018) is also the second named author of this paper; the conjecture originates from a prior 2018 work, not the present paper.
paper_title: Efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme for the genus of dense graphs

title: Open Problem (Spherical Density Regime)
statement_text: Determine whether efficient constant-factor approximation algorithms exist for the genus of graphs with average degree at most 6 (spherical density regime), or prove that approximating the genus in this regime is hard.
context_text: The genus $g(G)$ of a graph is the minimum genus of an orientable surface in which $G$ embeds; deciding whether $g(G)\le k$ is NP-complete (Thomassen), even for cubic graphs, and a constant-factor approximation means a polynomial-time algorithm producing an embedding (or an integer) within a constant factor of $g(G)$. Graphs whose genus is $\Theta(n)$, which includes graphs of average degree at least $d$ for some constant $d>6$, admit a constant-factor approximation by Euler's formula; the best known general algorithm (Kawarabayashi and Sidiropoulos) approximates the Euler genus within a factor $O(\hat g^{255}\log^{189}n)$, giving an $O(n^{1-\alpha})$ factor for the genus. Following an approach of Mohar, the authors split genus approximation into four regimes: spherical density (average degree at most 6), bounded average degree with hyperbolic density (average degree between constants $6<\delta<\Delta$, where a constant factor is easy but improving it may be hard), intermediate density (unbounded average degree and $o(n^2)$ edges), and dense graphs (at least $\alpha n^2$ edges), for which the paper gives an efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme. In the spherical density regime, described as probably the most interesting, there is no evidence that efficient constant-factor approximation algorithms exist, and resolving it is called the major open problem; Mohar (2018) conjectured that approximating the genus of cubic graphs is APX-hard, i.e. that approximation in this range is hard.
notes: Stated in prose: 'resolving this is the major open problem'; no formal labelled theorem environment.
paper_title: Efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme for the genus of dense graphs
